clue.text: Refuse facility ultimately lacking in Irish county

indicators.note: lacking in says the named letter is missing from the county's name

parts.note: Offaly is a county in the Irish midlands

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of facility

parts.note: its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip or waste plant is missing somewhere in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse facility' reads as one phrase (a dump), but Refuse alone is the definition; the Y that ends facility is dropped from OFFALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the waste parts of a butchered animal, so it is refuse in the sense of scraps thrown out.

clue.text: Wag from Bootle regularly entertaining small Liverpudlian chanteuse

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the others inside, as a host holds guests
regularly takes every other letter of Bootle

parts.note: Cilla Black was a singer from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A comedian from Bootle, a Merseyside town, often hosts a small singer from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Wag looks like a joker, fitting the Liverpool scene; it is the verb, to swing to and fro. Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool singer and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's tail wags by moving back and forth, which is to swing rhythmically from side to side.

clue.text: Facial expression of individual depressed by empty freezer?

indicators.note: depressed by means sitting below, so in this down clue the individual goes under the freezer letters
empty means the inside letters of freezer are removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: only its first and last letters are kept
own means individual, as in 'a room of one's own'

explanation.surface: A face pulled by someone left low by finding the freezer bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown is a furrowing of the brow showing displeasure, a look shown on the face.

clue.text: Eastern sailors continue briefly circling reef

indicators.note: circling means the shortened word goes around the reef
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to last is to continue or endure
a scar is a rocky outcrop, including one under the sea

explanation.surface: Sailors from the East keep going for a short while around a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascars were seamen from India or Southeast Asia employed on European ships.

clue.text: Shoots messenger at first when visiting state official investigating complaints

indicators.note: the shoots and letter are visiting, so they go inside the state's name

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula
buds are young shoots on a plant

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of messenger

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone guns down a courier while on a trip abroad, and a public watchdog takes an interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots messenger' suggests the proverb about not shooting the bearer of bad news; here shoots are plant growths, BUDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an appointed officer who looks into complaints made by the public against organisations.

clue.text: Exaggerate mounting neighbourhood revolt to some extent

indicators.note: mounting means rising, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards
to some extent means only a part of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Talking up a growing local uprising up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it too far or overstate it, which is what exaggerating does.

clue.text: Ship's officer, third to last leaving island country

indicators.note: leaving means the island's letter departs from the word
third to last means the third letter is sent to the end of the word

parts.note: a boatswain is the ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew

explanation.surface: A ship's officer, the third man in line, sets off from an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third to last' sounds like a ranking; it moves the third letter, A, to the end giving BOTSWAINA, and then the I goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa.

clue.text: Old Catholic enters seedy bar that attracts his condemnation?

definitions.text: Old Catholic enters seedy bar that attracts his condemnation?

indicators.note: enters puts the old Catholic letters inside the bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A traditional Catholic walks into a sleazy bar that draws his disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the Catholic Church condemns this, and the question mark admits the definition is a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman Catholic Church does not recognise the dissolution of a marriage, so a devout Catholic condemns it.

clue.text: Traditional Christmas food specimen I prepared

indicators.note: prepared, as food is, means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A sample of festive fare that I made.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince pies are small pastries filled with dried fruit and spices, eaten in Britain at Christmas.

clue.text: Working around Barking, one always on the move?

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the two letters are reversed

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
barking is British slang for mad, from 'barking mad'

explanation.surface: A busy person going round Barking, an east London district, never settles.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a place in east London, which makes the surface read as a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, travelling from place to place.

clue.text: Having had treatment, Scot with fewer wrinkles

indicators.note: letters that have been treated are worked over and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman, after a cosmetic procedure, has fewer lines on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about anti-ageing treatment, which makes 'wrinkles' feel like part of the story rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine creases at the outer corners of the eyes, a common type of facial line.

clue.text: Number imprisoned by extremely vile Frenchman showing spite

indicators.note: imprisoned by puts the number inside the surrounding letters
extremely takes the outermost letters of vile

parts.note: its first and last letters are used
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A spiteful French villain locks up some numbered prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom figuratively means bitter malice or hostility, close in sense to spite.

clue.text: Stuff covering some rope

indicators.note: covering means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to lard is to stuff meat with fat, so stuff can mean lard
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Some material is used to wrap a length of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short cord or line, used on ships for securing things or around the neck to hold a whistle.

clue.text: Part of torpedo roll bird's tucked into

indicators.note: tucked into puts the bird inside the roll

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A bird has burrowed into a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The warhead is the front section of a torpedo or missile that carries the explosive charge.

clue.text: Settle bill exactly

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, which a bill or poster can be
just means exactly, as in 'just so'

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay a bill to the penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle bill' looks like paying an account; bill is in fact a poster, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a mechanism or arrangement is to adjust it, fixing it into the right position.

clue.text: Observing American sportsman's superior manoeuvring

indicators.note: superior means above, so in a down clue the sportsman sits on top

parts.note: in the US a jock is an athlete; the 's stands for 'is'
eying is a spelling of eyeing, observing

explanation.surface: Watching an American athlete's boss making moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeying is skilful manoeuvring for position or advantage, as riders do in a race.

clue.text: Succeeds with prison pardon Northern Ireland rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the assembled letters are turned back to front

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
'eh?' is a way of saying 'pardon?' when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Someone wins, with a jail release refused by Northern Ireland's authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Pardon here is not a legal release but the query 'eh?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to succeed to a title or property as an heir, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Hare bolts, worrying large mammal

indicators.note: worrying means harrying or tearing at, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A hare runs off, alarming a big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth bear is a shaggy bear of the Indian subcontinent, a sizeable mammal.

clue.text: Singers collectively meditated, some said it provides calm

indicators.note: some said means the words sound like the answer to some speakers

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers; chewed, as in chewed over, means thought about or meditated

explanation.surface: A choir meditated together, which some claim brings serenity.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'choir chewed' sounds like the answer; 'some' admits it works only in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Quietude is a state of stillness and peace, a noun sense of calm.

clue.text: Eulogy once performed by parent, inspiring one

indicators.note: performed means the letters of once are worked into a new order
inspiring means breathing in, so the parent takes the one inside

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A tribute speech once delivered by a mother who encouraged someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or text of high praise, the same idea as a eulogy.

clue.text: Set up office divided by metal screen

indicators.note: set up means raised, so in this down clue the whole is read upwards
divided by means the metal splits the room's letters

parts.note: an office is a room where work is done
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Establishing a workplace partitioned by a metal panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a computer display, the screen on which output is shown.

clue.text: Conservative, originally opposed, is backing new detailed artwork

indicators.note: the Conservative and the letter are backing, standing behind, the shortened word
detailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of opposed

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A Tory, initially against it, now supports a new intricate painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed artwork' reads as an intricate picture, but detailed is the instruction to drop the H from FRESH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting done on wet plaster, so it is a work of art.

clue.text: Went to pit and changed to slicks, as told over the radio?

indicators.note: told over the radio means heard rather than read, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: slicks are smooth racing tyres, so a car changed to them has been re-tyred

explanation.surface: A racing driver came into the pits and switched tyres, as relayed on team radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit looks like the motor racing pit lane; it is slang for bed, so 'went to pit' is went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night, and pit is British slang for one's bed.

clue.text: Authority imposed around India that is unrestricted

indicators.note: around means the imposed letters sit either side

parts.note: put means placed or imposed, as in put upon

indicators.note: unrestricted means without its limits, so the outer letters of India go

parts.note: its middle letters are used

explanation.surface: A rule enforced across India that has no limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an expert, someone who speaks as an authority on a subject.

clue.text: Disinfect beds in same place, occasionally all over

indicators.note: all over means turned over, so the chosen letters are read backwards
occasionally means only every other letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: An instruction to sanitise beds kept in one spot, now and then right through.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse something is to make it thoroughly clean, which is what disinfecting does.

clue.text: Overlooking some French titled lady for musical

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman with a title
du is French for 'some', as in du pain

explanation.surface: A French noblewoman being ignored in favour of a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters.

clue.text: Follow track cycling story

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to hunt is to follow or pursue
a rut is a track worn in the ground

explanation.surface: A sporting instruction to tail a velodrome cycling event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track cycling' looks like the sport; cycling instead sends the H at the front of HUNTRUT to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A story, in the sense of a fib told to cover something up, is a lie or falsehood.

clue.text: Discovered cause of sore feet is rugby, maybe?

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: Someone has found that their aching feet come from playing rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the sport generally; it is one form of a code named with this word, rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby union is one code of rugby, so rugby can be an example of a union.

clue.text: Live with bigoted character needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sexist is a person prejudiced against one sex

explanation.surface: Putting up with a prejudiced person who is so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' is a stock phrase for someone famous; here it removes the opening S.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive and have being, so it can replace live as a verb.

clue.text: Stress evident in Victoria, perhaps lower than before

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: under means lower than
the Victoria line is one London Underground line, an example of a line

explanation.surface: Strain is apparent in someone named Victoria, maybe more down than previously.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like a woman; it is the Victoria line on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, so the verb means stress.

clue.text: Suspect grubs ate hedges close to vegetable crop

indicators.note: hedges means fences in, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are in a doubtful, rearranged order
close to takes the final letter of vegetable

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Larvae are thought to have eaten hedgerows next to a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedges' looks like the plants the grubs ate, and 'vegetable crop' like one phrase; hedges is the containment signal and only crop defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is a root grown on a field scale in temperate countries to produce sugar, an agricultural crop.

clue.text: Algerian ready at home before American doctor rings

indicators.note: rings means the doctor's letters surround the others
before puts the home letters ahead of the American one

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: An Algerian, prepared and at home, waits before an American doctor's phone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for cash (as in 'readies'), so 'Algerian ready' is Algeria's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of Algeria, so it is Algerian cash.
